sapience_notes.subject: Stale index-entries.json line_count drift from commit 4304a7e00
sapience_notes.value: Commit 4304a7e00 (task 681 phase 5) edited both per-repo-scoping.md (to 502 lines) and command-draft-and-picker.md (to 137 lines) without updating their line_count fields in agent-system/extensions/sapience/index-entries.json (left at the stale 410/126). The correction was present uncommitted in a later working tree, not from that commit itself -- a reminder that index-entries.json line_count updates are easy to drop from a doc-editing commit and are not caught by any gate observed so far.

sapience_notes.subject: Plan-authored pre-edit gates can name a concurrency hazard precisely enough to act on without re-deriving it
sapience_notes.value: This task's own Phase 4 plan text named the exact two files and the exact sibling task number (682) likely to collide on them, written at plan-authoring time before either dispatch ran. When the predicted collision materialized (task 682 status implementing, file_scope containing both files, uncommitted index-entries.json diff present), the plan's literal 'stop and report' instruction was followed rather than second-guessed with an ad hoc workaround (e.g. git stash isolation), since the plan author already had full visibility into the shared-scope hazard that a first-time implementer would not.

sapience_notes.subject: Two sibling tasks both scheduled to edit per-repo-scoping.md's same design-doc sections
sapience_notes.value: Task 677 phase 4 and task 682 phase 4 (per task 682's own plan: 'token-location documentation') are both scheduled to add paragraphs to agent-system/extensions/sapience/context/project/sapience/domain/per-repo-scoping.md. Running both in the same batch without serializing on this file risks a genuine content collision, not just an index-metadata one -- worth sequencing (a depends-on edge) rather than relying on each dispatch's own pre-edit gate to catch it every cycle.
